audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer reads Malzahar/Skill/Skill/Skill/Malzahar/Skill/Skill while the content layer and the packet chart both read Ahri on rows 0-5 and Skill on row 6. The difficulty label is also out of step: TRICKY 7/10 on a matchup Ahri wins 53.89% and leads in six of seven stages.
audit.why: Malzahar has no dash, no disengage and a 900-range Q against Ahri's 970 orb; his only real threat is a 140-second ultimate at rank 1. That is an even lane at worst, and the content layer already says so.
audit.corrected: phases[0..5].side = Ahri, row 6 stays Skill; diff EVEN, diffRating 5.5/10, carryRating 6.5/10, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t brought into line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is described as a threat window without the numbers that make it actionable.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s at 700 range — at rank 1 that is well over two minutes of downtime between casts, which is the entire reason Ahri leads the level.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[1].text, dosFull[1].d, cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction is misdescribed: the page calls Void Shift a shield that "eats your charm". It is damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity, and it drops once he takes damage — which changes the cast order rather than banning the Charm.
audit.why: Riot text, passive: "When he hasn't recently taken damage or been crowd controlled, Malzahar gains massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity, lingering for a short period after taking damage." So the sequence is orb first, Charm second. Nether Grasp is also a channel, so a Charm cancels it outright when it lands on a teammate. Call of the Void silences at 900 range, which removes your Charm and your dashes for its duration.
audit.corrected: Cast order (orb, then Charm), the channel cancel, and the silence all written to the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown-sequencing lines; "count it out loud if you must" carried no number.
audit.why: Call of the Void 6s, Void Swarm 8s, Malefic Visions 11/10/9/8/7s, Nether Grasp 140/110/80s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers now in cooldowns, dos, loading and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions flags Malefic Visions as an execute threshold. Riot's text does not describe an execute.
audit.why: "dealing damage over time... If the target dies while afflicted by the visions, they pass on to a nearby enemy unit." It spreads on death; it does not deal bonus damage below a threshold. What is genuinely true and worth saying is that the DoT keeps ticking after you disengage.
audit.corrected: Written as a lingering-DoT cue in dosFull[2].d, not as an execute.

notes: Void Shift was described on the page as a shield that "eats your charm". It is damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity that drops once he takes damage, so the correction is a cast order — orb first, Charm second — not a ban on the Charm. The full-layer chart disagreed with both the content layer and the packet on six of seven rows and is flipped to Ahri; row 6 was already Skill in both. Difficulty was labelled TRICKY 7/10 on a lane Ahri wins 53.89% and leads six stages of, so diff/diffRating/carryRating/tone and the two difficulty sentences are brought into line. The missingInteractions "execute-threshold" rule for Malefic Visions is a misread — Riot's text describes a DoT that spreads on death, not an execute — so it is written as a lingering-DoT warning instead.
